formation.title: The Restoration of Byzantium
formation.text:
The eagles of Rome fly once more over Constantinople. The ancient capital, seat of emperors for a thousand years, has been reclaimed for Greek civilization and the Orthodox faith. The Hagia Sophia's dome catches the light of a new dawn.

But what shall this restored empire be? The legacy of Rome offers two visions. One looks to Justinian and the Caesars, a universal empire of law, discipline, and conquest, where the Basileus rules as God's chosen administrator of earthly affairs. The other looks to the Ecumenical Patriarch and the Desert Fathers, a sacred commonwealth where Orthodoxy unites the peoples, where monasteries preserve civilization, and where spiritual authority outshines any temporal crown.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are Rome reborn. By law and sword we shall rule

modifiers.name: Renovatio Imperii
modifiers.text: The Roman Empire has been restored. As heirs to Augustus and Justinian, the Basileus claims dominion over the civilized world through law, administration, and military might.

options.text: We are the light of Orthodoxy. Faith shall be our empire

modifiers.name: The Orthodox Ecumene
modifiers.text: Constantinople stands once more as the spiritual center of Christendom. The Ecumenical Patriarch's authority radiates from the Hagia Sophia, drawing the faithful into the embrace of Orthodoxy.

options.text: The old gods favor us. Under the Olympians, Rome shall rise

modifiers.name: The Hellenic Revival
modifiers.text: The old gods return to their temples. With Constantinople restored not to Christ but to the Olympians, the Basileus revives the imperial cult, the omens, and the academies of antiquity. Rome looks to its most ancient roots.

advances.name: Greek Fire
advances.text: The secret of liquid fire that burns upon water, projected from bronze siphons on war galleys.

event.title: The Weapon of Emperors
event.text:
The secret of Greek fire, the liquid flame that burns upon water, was perhaps the most closely guarded state secret in all of history. Invented by Kallinikos of Heliopolis in the 7th century, it was projected from bronze siphons mounted on the prows of dromons, turning Byzantine warships into floating flamethrowers.

The composition was known only to a handful of craftsmen whose families passed the formula down through generations. No enemy ever replicated it. The mere rumor that a Byzantine fleet carried siphons was often enough to prevent battle entirely. Arab, Russian, and Bulgar fleets all learned to fear the terrible cry of 'Loose the fire!' that preceded sheets of liquid flame racing across the sea.

options.text: The flame of empire burns eternal

modifiers.name: Greek Fire Mastery
modifiers.text: The secret of liquid fire has been perfected. Our galleys carry siphons that project inextinguishable flame across the waves, turning every naval engagement into a conflagration.

advances.name: Thematic Administration
advances.text: The theme system divided the empire into military-administrative districts where soldier-farmers defended the land they tilled.

advances.name: Pronoia System
advances.text: Land grants to military officers in exchange for cavalry service, the Byzantine answer to Western feudalism.

advances.name: Imperial Silk Monopoly
advances.text: State-controlled silk workshops producing the finest textiles in the world, with Tyrian purple reserved for the emperor alone.

advances.name: Stradioti Tradition
advances.text: The tradition of Greek and Albanian light cavalry raiders, famed across Europe for their speed and ferocity.

advances.name: Imperial Neoria
advances.text: The great dockyards of the Golden Horn, where the dromon fleet was built and maintained.

advances.name: Cistern Engineering
advances.text: The art of building vast underground reservoirs that sustained Constantinople through siege and drought.

event.title: Constantinople Restored
event.text:
For a thousand years, Constantinople was the greatest city in Christendom, perhaps in the world. Its triple walls defied every siege. Its underground cisterns, like the great Basilica Cistern with its 336 marble columns, held enough fresh water to sustain the population through months of blockade. Its position on the Bosphorus controlled the passage between Europe and Asia, between the Mediterranean and the Black Sea.

Now the city is being rebuilt. Engineers restore the aqueducts of Valens, workers clear the debris from the great forums, and the markets of the Mese begin to fill once more with goods from distant lands. The question is whether to make Constantinople an impregnable fortress or an irresistible market.

options.text: Make the walls invincible. No enemy shall pass

modifiers.name: The Queen of Cities Restored
modifiers.text: Constantinople's walls stand firm once more. The great cisterns fill with fresh water, the aqueducts carry life through every quarter, and the city resumes its ancient role as the most fortified metropolis in the world.

options.text: Open the gates to commerce. Let gold flow like water

modifiers.name: A New Golden Age
modifiers.text: Constantinople's markets bustle once more with the trade of three continents. Merchants from Venice, Genoa, Egypt, and the Rus converge on the Golden Horn, and the empire's coffers swell with the wealth of the crossroads.

advances.name: Book of the Eparch
advances.text: The Byzantine trade regulation manual governing Constantinople's guilds, from silk weavers to perfumers.

advances.name: Hippodrome Tradition
advances.text: The hippodrome was the political heart of the empire, where chariot factions served as proto-parties and emperors secured popular legitimacy.

advances.name: Justinianic Legal Revival
advances.text: Drawing on the Corpus Juris Civilis to build an efficient centralized administration rooted in Roman legal tradition.

event.title: The Revival of Justinian's Law
event.text:
The Corpus Juris Civilis, the Body of Civil Law, was Justinian's greatest monument, more enduring than the Hagia Sophia itself. Compiled between 529 and 534 by the jurist Tribonian and his team, it codified a thousand years of Roman legal thought into a coherent system that addressed marriage, property, inheritance, criminal law, and the rights of citizens.

Though the original empire that produced this masterwork fell, its legal principles survived. They were studied in the universities of Bologna and Paris, and they shaped the civil law tradition of half of Europe. Now, a restored Byzantine state draws upon this heritage to build an administration that combines ancient Roman efficiency with the needs of a modern empire.

options.text: Justice is the foundation of empire

modifiers.name: Justinianic Legacy
modifiers.text: The revival of Justinian's legal codex has brought order to the empire's administration. Courts follow written law, tax collectors answer to magistrates, and the machinery of Roman governance turns once more.

advances.name: Phanariote Diplomacy
advances.text: The Phanariote Greeks served as administrators, interpreters, and diplomats across the eastern Mediterranean, masters of intrigue and negotiation.

advances.name: Neo-Byzantine Enlightenment
advances.text: A renaissance of learning drawing on classical and Byzantine scholarship, transforming education and governance.

advances.name: Imperial Naval Modernization
advances.text: The transition from galley-based warfare to a modern fleet, combining ancient maritime tradition with contemporary ship design.

destiny.name: Destiny of Byzantium
destiny.text: The empire has been restored. Now it must prove itself worthy of the name of Rome.

event.title: The Destiny of Byzantium
event.text: The restored empire stands at a crossroads of history. Constantinople's walls have been rebuilt, the Hagia Sophia rings once more with Orthodox liturgy, and the eagle standard flies over the Bosphorus. But restoration is only the beginning. The empire that once stretched from Spain to Mesopotamia cannot rest content with what it holds. What direction shall Byzantium's destiny take?

options.text: Our destiny awaits

destiny.name: Reclaim the Exarchate
destiny.text: The Exarchate of Ravenna was Byzantium's western anchor for centuries. Take Ravenna and Bari to re-establish imperial authority in Italy.

conditions.text: Own Ravenna, or a subject owns it
Own Bari, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Exarchate Reclaimed
event.text:
The Exarchate of Ravenna was established in 584 as Byzantium's administrative center in Italy, governing the remnants of Justinian's reconquest. For nearly two centuries it held the line against Lombards and Franks, preserving Roman civilization in the West. Its loss in 751 to the Lombards marked the end of Byzantine authority in central Italy.

Now Ravenna and Bari fly the imperial standard once more. The mosaics of San Vitale, depicting Justinian and Theodora in all their imperial glory, look down upon Byzantine soldiers for the first time in centuries.

options.text: Italy remembers its Roman masters

destiny.name: Reconquista Africana
destiny.text: Justinian's reconquest of North Africa from the Vandals was one of his greatest triumphs. Follow in his footsteps by taking Tunis and Tripoli.

conditions.text: Own Tunis, or a subject owns it
Own Tripoli, or a subject owns it

event.title: Africa Reconquered
event.text:
In 533, Belisarius landed in Africa with just 15,000 men and, in a campaign of astonishing brilliance, destroyed the Vandal kingdom in a matter of months. The African provinces became Rome's breadbasket once more, their grain feeding Constantinople for another century.

Now history repeats itself. Byzantine banners fly over Carthage's ruins and Tripoli's harbor. The question is how to use this reconquest, as a military springboard for further expansion, or as an agricultural heartland to feed the empire's growing population.

options.text: Raise African legions for the campaigns ahead

modifiers.name: African Legions
modifiers.text: The reconquered African provinces supply fresh recruits for the imperial army, raising new legions in the tradition of Belisarius's African campaign.

options.text: Let Africa feed the empire as it once fed Rome

modifiers.name: African Granary
modifiers.text: Africa's fertile plains resume their ancient role as the empire's breadbasket, their harvests feeding Constantinople and fueling growth.

destiny.name: Renovatio Imperii
destiny.text: The full restoration of the Roman Empire: Rome, Antioch, Alexandria. Three of the five ancient pentarchies united under one eagle. This is the ultimate capstone of the Heir of Rome.

conditions.text: Own Rome, or a subject owns it
Own Antioch, or a subject owns it
Own Alexandria, or a subject owns it

event.title: Renovatio Imperii
event.text:
Rome. Antioch. Alexandria. Three of the five great patriarchates of ancient Christendom now answer to Constantinople. The Mediterranean is once more a Roman lake. This is the achievement that Justinian dreamed of, that Heraclius fought for, that the Palaiologoi mourned as forever lost.

The Renovatio Imperii, the Renewal of the Empire, is complete. But every great empire must choose how to sustain its greatness. Will the restored Rome bring peace and order to its subjects through law and administration? Or will it maintain its dominion through the invincible legions that won this empire?

options.text: Let Roman law bring order to the world

modifiers.name: Pax Romana
modifiers.text: Roman law and administration bring peace and order to the vast domains of the restored empire, reducing unrest and binding subjects through justice rather than force.

options.text: The legions are eternal. They are the empire

modifiers.name: Eternal Legions
modifiers.text: The legions that conquered three continents remain the backbone of imperial power, their discipline and speed unmatched by any rival army.

destiny.name: The Ecumenical See
destiny.text: Ohrid, the archbishopric that Basil II set over the Bulgarian lands, and Jerusalem, the holiest city in Christendom. Secure these sacred seats to establish the spiritual authority of the Orthodox Ecumene.

conditions.text: Own Ohrid, or a subject owns it
Own Jerusalem, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Ecumenical See
event.text:
Ohrid, seat of the archbishops whom Basil II set over the Bulgarian lands, and Jerusalem, the holiest site in Christendom, both acknowledge the authority of the Ecumenical Patriarch. The spiritual geography of Orthodoxy now radiates from Constantinople in all directions, west to the Balkans, south to the Holy Land, north to the Slavic world.

Monasteries flourish, pilgrim routes multiply, and the Orthodox faithful look to the New Rome as their spiritual center. The foundation of a sacred commonwealth has been laid.

options.text: The faithful gather under the Patriarch's wing

destiny.name: The Orthodox Commonwealth
destiny.text: Build a thriving economic and cultural commonwealth. Dominate the silk trade in your capital market, and let Thessaloniki, the second city, grow rich again on the fair of Saint Demetrius, where the merchants of the Slavic lands gather.

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

conditions.text: We own Thessaloniki and its development is at least 37

event.title: The Orthodox Commonwealth
event.text:
The empire's markets overflow with silk, spice, and the products of three continents. At Thessaloniki the fair of Saint Demetrius is crowded again with merchants from the Slavic lands. The trade that once enriched Venice and Genoa now passes through Byzantine harbours. The old Silk Road routes that made Constantinople the wealthiest city in the medieval world have been restored, and the capital's market dominates the eastern Mediterranean.

This prosperity can be directed in different ways. The wealth of trade can spread Byzantine culture across the known world, or the monasteries can use this golden age to advance Orthodox learning and scholarship.

options.text: Let our culture flow with our trade

modifiers.name: Silk Road Restored
modifiers.text: The ancient trade routes that made Constantinople wealthy beyond measure flow once more, spreading Byzantine culture and wealth across the known world.

options.text: The monasteries shall be beacons of learning

modifiers.name: Monastic Learning
modifiers.text: The great monasteries of Athos, Sinai, and the Studion become centers of scholarship, preserving and advancing knowledge in the Orthodox tradition.

destiny.name: The New Rome
destiny.text: Constantinople becomes the New Rome in truth, the cultural, spiritual, and intellectual capital of the world. Open a library in the City, fill the empty quarters within the Theodosian walls until the City is twice what it was, and prove that Byzantium's light outshines all rivals.

conditions.text: We own Constantinople and it has a Library
We own Constantinople and its development is at least 62

event.title: The New Rome
event.text:
Constantinople is no longer merely the capital of a restored empire; it is the intellectual and spiritual center of the world. The Patriarchal Academy produces scholars and theologians who rival the best of any university in Europe. From the City's library, Orthodox texts and Greek philosophy go out across the continent. Byzantine art, architecture, and thought set the standard for civilization itself.

This is the New Rome that the founders of Constantinople dreamed of, not merely a political capital, but a beacon of civilization. The question is whether to emphasize its role as the sacred center of Orthodoxy, or as the commercial crossroads of the known world.

options.text: Orthodoxy shall illuminate the world

modifiers.name: Beacon of Faith
modifiers.text: Orthodoxy radiates from Constantinople as a spiritual beacon, its moral authority drawing the faithful and overawing the heathen.

effects.name: Damage Done versus Heathens in Battle

options.text: Constantinople is the crossroads of worlds

modifiers.name: Crossroads of Worlds
modifiers.text: Constantinople commands the junction of Europe and Asia, its harbors and markets linking the trade of the entire world.

destiny.name: The Temples Reopened
destiny.text: With the old gods restored, their altars must rise again. Reconsecrate the temples of Athens, the cradle of the Olympian faith, and let the smoke of sacrifice and the voice of the oracles guide the reborn empire.

conditions.text: Own Athína, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Temples Reopened
event.text: The Olympian gods return to their altars. Across the empire, temples that stood silent for a thousand years ring once more with hymns and the smoke of sacrifice. The oracles speak, the omens are read, and the ancient faith of Greece and Rome is reborn under the Basileus who dared restore it.

options.text: The gods have come home

destiny.name: The Academy Restored
destiny.text: The wisdom of antiquity returns. Reopen Plato's Academy at Athens with a library of its own and the great schools of Ionia at Smyrna, and let Athens grow from a ducal town into a city of scholars, so that philosophy, mathematics, and the classical sciences flourish once more.

conditions.text: We own Athens and it has a Library
We own Athens and its development is at least 44
Own Smyrna, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Academy Restored
event.text: The wisdom of antiquity flowers anew. In Athens, Plato's Academy reopens its gates; in Ionia, the schools of Smyrna draw scholars from across the world. But the classical revival can take two forms: the rigorous natural sciences of Aristotle's Lyceum, or the philosophy, rhetoric, and art of the Painted Stoa.

options.text: The Lyceum: let reason and science lead

modifiers.name: The Lyceum
modifiers.text: Aristotle's school of natural philosophy reborn: the sciences, medicine, and engineering of antiquity drive the empire's advancement and its great works.

options.text: The Stoa: let philosophy and art adorn the empire

modifiers.name: The Painted Stoa
modifiers.text: The porch where Zeno taught: philosophy, rhetoric, and the arts flourish, and the cultured prestige of Hellas radiates through the empire's diplomacy.

destiny.name: Apotheosis
destiny.text: The classical world is whole again. With Athens and the sanctuary of Olympia held, the Basileus is acclaimed among the gods, the Olympic games unite the empire, and the civilization of antiquity stands reborn in eternal glory. The capstone of the Hellenic Renaissance.

conditions.text: Own Athína, or a subject owns it
Own Pontikokastro, or a subject owns it

event.title: Apotheosis
event.text: The classical world stands whole again, and the Basileus is acclaimed not merely as emperor but as a living god, heir to Augustus and to Alexander. The golden age of antiquity is reborn. Shall the empire be bound together by the divine imperial cult, or by the restored Olympic games that draw all Greeks into one sacred festival?

options.text: Let the Imperial Cult sanctify our rule

modifiers.name: The Imperial Cult
modifiers.text: The Basileus is worshipped as a living god. The divine emperor's golden age fills the treasury and raises monuments across the reborn classical world.

options.text: Let the Eternal Olympiad unite the Hellenes

modifiers.name: The Eternal Olympiad
modifiers.text: The sacred games of Olympia are restored, drawing all Greeks into one festival of the gods. The priesthoods are content, the provinces are quiet, and people come from afar to settle where the games are held.

units.name: Dromon
units.text: The dromon was the backbone of the Byzantine navy, a fast, oar-driven war galley equipped with a bronze siphon for projecting Greek fire. Its crew of rowers and marines made it a versatile instrument of naval power in the confined waters of the Aegean and the Straits.

units.name: Pronoiarioi
units.text: Cavalrymen who hold a pronoia, the revenue of a district granted for as long as they serve. They ride in mail and lamellar with lance and bow, lighter than a Western knight and steadier under orders.

units.name: Stradioti
units.text: Light cavalry recruited from the Albanian and Greek borderlands, the Stradioti were swift raiders and scouts whose javelin-armed charges could shatter an exposed flank. They served as mercenaries across Europe, hired by Venice, France, and Spain.

units.name: Imperial Fire Dromon
units.text: The apex of Byzantine naval design, a heavy dromon with reinforced hull and an advanced Greek fire siphon system. These warships controlled the narrow waters of the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles, their liquid fire making them nearly unstoppable in close combat.

units.name: Pyrpolikon
units.text: A fireship: a small fast brig packed with pitch and powder, sailed alongside an enemy ship of the line and set alight. The islanders who crew it are the last heirs of Greek fire.

buildings.name: Imperial Cistern
buildings.text: A vast underground reservoir modeled on Constantinople's legendary Basilica Cistern, with hundreds of marble columns supporting a vaulted ceiling above millions of gallons of fresh water.

buildings.name: Silk Ergasterion
buildings.text: An imperial silk workshop where raw silk is spun, dyed with precious pigments, and woven into the finest textiles in the world. The purple silk of the Basileus is produced here.

buildings.name: Imperial Hippodrome
buildings.text: A monumental arena for chariot racing and public ceremonies. The hippodrome served as the political heart of the empire, where factions clashed and emperors were acclaimed.

buildings.name: Byzantine Neorion
buildings.text: An imperial naval dockyard on the model of Constantinople's Golden Horn arsenals, where dromons are built, repaired, and fitted with their deadly siphons of liquid fire.

buildings.name: Imperial Triumph
buildings.text: A monumental triumphal complex celebrating the restoration of Rome, combining the grandeur of ancient imperial forums with Byzantine administrative efficiency.

buildings.name: Patriarchal Academy
buildings.text: A center of Orthodox theological and philosophical learning, heir to the ancient Pandidakterion, producing scholars, scribes, and diplomats.

buildings.name: The Pantheon Restored
buildings.text: A great temple to the Twelve Olympians, its altars tended by the revived priesthood. From here the old faith spreads anew and the classical culture of the empire radiates outward.

list.name: Synodos Endemousa
list.text: The endemousa synodos was the permanent council of bishops resident at Constantinople, presided over by the Ecumenical Patriarch. Functioning continuously from the early Byzantine centuries through 1453, the standing synod ruled on canon law, dogma, marriages of the great families, and questions affecting the whole Orthodox world from the Balkans to Antioch. Its decisions bound the eastern Church and gave the Patriarchate corporate authority outside the throne, a parallel legitimacy the basileus could lean on, but never wholly command.

list.name: Genikon Logothesion
list.text: The genikon, the General Treasury, was the central fiscal bureau of the middle-Byzantine state from the seventh century onward, headed by the logothetes tou genikou. Its chartoularioi maintained the tax registers in Constantinople; its epoptai audited the themes; its tribunal heard fiscal cases. Where the Basilika codified law and the Allelengyon levied collective burden, the genikon was the auditing engine itself: the bureau that hunted arrears, recovered exemptions, and stripped magnate fictions from the cadasters.

list.name: Office of the Mesazon
list.text: The mesazon (literally 'the intermediary') emerged formally as a state office at the Empire of Nicaea and was inherited by the restored Palaiologan empire, where figures like Demetrios Kydones and the last mesazon Loukas Notaras coordinated policy day and night for the basileus. A single trusted technocrat between the throne and the rest of the administration, the mesazon centralised in a way the dignity-laden senatorial titulature never could, and aroused the resentment of the great houses whose precedence it bypassed.

funded.name: Head of the Cabinet Promotion Cost Modifier

list.name: Eparchate of Constantinople
list.text: The Eparch of Constantinople was called 'father of the city' and ranked just beneath the emperor himself. As supreme judge of the capital, master of its guilds (whose regulation Leo VI codified in the Book of the Eparch), and overseer of grain supply, fire-watch, and street discipline, the prefect kept the world's largest city fed and orderly. The dynatoi resented an officer whose authority within the walls outranked their own; the people called on him whenever bread or justice ran short.

list.name: Mystikos and the Asecretis
list.text: The mystikos ('the secret one') served as the basileus's private secretary from the ninth century, controlling the imperial seal alongside the keeper of the inkstand and supervising the asecretis, the inner-cabinet scribes. Under Manuel I Komnenos the office grew to command the palace and the privy purse. A discreet apparatus parallel to the public chancery, the mystikos handled sensitive correspondence, internal investigations, and the throne's own intelligence, to the unease of the patriarch, whose ecclesiastical jurisdiction it could quietly skirt.
